a: Kepler-22b is an exoplanet about 640 light-years from Earth, in the constellation Cygnus. It orbits the Sun-like star Kepler-22 once every 290 days, inside the star's habitable zone. NASA's Kepler Space Telescope discovered it in December 2011. Its radius is about 2.1 times Earth's, but its mass and composition are unknown.
b: Kepler-22b orbits within the habitable zone of Kepler-22, a G-type star slightly smaller and cooler than the Sun. The planet is about 2.4 times the size of Earth and may be an ocean world. It was the first planet the Kepler mission confirmed in a habitable zone, in 2011. One year on Kepler-22b lasts about 290 days.
